# Releases

The current stable threadneedle release is 7.4.1. Every tagged release follows, newest first.

## 7.4.1 (2026-08-19)

Patch release. Fixes a scheduler stall when a worker pool shrinks below its reserved capacity. No configuration changes.

## 7.4.0 (2026-07-02)

- New `threadneedle queue inspect` command.
- Behaviour change: delayed jobs now count against the queue depth limit.

## 7.3.4 (2026-05-15)

- Fixed: retry backoff no longer skips the first interval.

## 7.3.0 (2025-11-21)

- Added per-task rate limits.

Releases older than 7.3 are listed in the archive.

web_fixture.title: Upgrading to threadneedle 7.3.0: what changed for us
web_fixture.snippet: A month after moving our invoice pipeline onto the 7.3 line, we wrote down what actually changed and what we would do differently.
web_fixture.content:
# Upgrading to threadneedle 7.3.0: what changed for us

*Posted 2025-12-02 by Callum Fenwick - Unwin Operations engineering notes*

We moved our invoice pipeline onto the 7.3 line in late November and have stayed there through the winter.

## What we run

Three scheduler nodes and eleven workers per region, all on the 7.3.x line. We pinned 7.3.0 and have not taken a patch since; nothing in the 7.3 series after that touched anything we use.

## The migration itself

The upgrade was uneventful. We drained each worker, swapped the binary, and let the queue refill.

## What we would change

Nothing about the version, honestly. Our next move is a review of the retry policies, not the broker.

*Callum Fenwick runs platform reliability at Unwin Operations.*

web_fixture.snippet: A durable task queue with at-least-once delivery, delayed jobs, and a single binary scheduler.
web_fixture.content:
# threadneedle

A durable task queue for clusters that do not want a managed service. At-least-once delivery, delayed jobs, per-task rate limits, and a single binary scheduler backed by Postgres or SQLite.

- At-least-once delivery with visible retry state
- Delayed and scheduled jobs
- Per-task rate limits
- One binary; scheduler and worker modes

## Getting started

```
brew install threadneedle
threadneedle init --store postgres://localhost/queue
threadneedle worker --pool invoices
```

## Status

The project is maintained by a small group of operators. Tagged releases and their notes are published on threadneedle.io; the changelog in this repository mirrors them.

MIT licensed.
